entries.title: Psalms 72:1
segments:
Thy judgments; thy righteous decisions. 
 
  The king's son; literally, Solomon, so called as the son of David and his successor on the throne, in correspondence with the original promise of God to David, "He shall build a house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever,"

; the words include the entire line of Solomon's successors, which is perpetuated for ever in Christ.  Thus Christ himself is the main subject of the psalm.  In Solomon it has only an incipient fulfilment. 
 
All wise decisions and all righteous conduct proceed from God their author; and to him all should look that he would grant them the influence of his grace, and thus fit them for the various duties to which they are called.

entries.title: Psalms 72:3
segments: The mountains shall bring peace--by righteousness; the mountains and hills shall, as it were, bring forth a harvest of peace to God's people, as the effect of righteousness.  Peace includes in itself all prosperity, temporal and spiritual.  Righteousness is here the righteous government of the king whom this psalm celebrated, producing righteousness among the people.

entries.title: Psalms 72:4
segments: The kingdom of Christ, with the salvation which it brings to the soul, is the heritage of none but the poor in spirit.  The proud and self sufficient are excluded from it, and must stumble and fall into perdition.

entries.title: Psalms 72:6
segments: He shall come down; the effect of his righteous administration shall be like that of rain on meadows newly mown.  Compare
.  The happy effects of Solomon's just and peaceable reign were typical of the nobler influences of Christ's spiritual reign over his people.

entries.title: Psalms 72:7
segments: Since the cause of the righteous is the cause of Christ, it must increase and prosper until it becomes triumphant over the whole earth; and, during its conflict with the kingdom of Satan, all that are spiritually united to Christ, enjoy, in the midst of their outward trials, the peace of God which passeth all understanding.

entries.title: Psalms 72:8
segments: From sea to sea; over all the earth.

entries.title: Psalms 72:9
segments: Lick the dust; be utterly subdued.

entries.title: Psalms 72:10
segments:
vv 10-11. 
 
  Tarshish--the isles--Sheba and Seba; Tarshish was a celebrated mart of trade in the south-west of Spain.  The isles are, in general, the sea-coasts and islands of the Mediterranean.  Sheba was a country of Southern Arabia, celebrated for its gold, spices, and precious stones.

Seba is generally supposed to have been Meroe, a province of Ethiopia.  These countries stand here to represent all the nations of the earth, which shall in due time give their wealth and homage to Christ.  Compare

entries.title: Psalms 72:12
segments:
vv 12-13. 
 
  He shall deliver the needy; the protection which Solomon as a righteous king gave to the poor and needy, represented the higher spiritual protection which Christ gives to all the poor in spirit, who feel their need of him and come to him for help and salvation.  Compare

. 
 
Whatever may be the outward worldly condition of Christ's disciples, he will give them all needful protection, help, and comfort here, and eternal deliverance from all oppression and sorrow hereafter.

entries.title: Psalms 72:15
segments:
For him; for the extension of his blessed kingdom in the world, and in the heart of him who offers the prayer. 
 
All the true members of Christ's body are animated by his spirit, which is the spirit of love and self-denial.  They continually pray for his honor and the enlargement of his kingdom among men; and to this end give liberally of that which God has entrusted to them.

entries.title: Psalms 72:16
segments: Upon the top of the mountains; upon the most unlikely places, as well as others, the gospel shall take deep root and produce abundant fruits.

entries.title: Psalms 72:20
segments: Are ended; this is the close of the second of the books into which the Psalms were anciently divided.
